info.title: Shipshape REST API
info.description:
Everything the Shipshape portal's pages can do, as JSON. Every page and every form operation in the UI has an
endpoint here (a test walks the site's routes and templates to keep it that way), and each one calls the same
code and validates with the same forms as the page, so the API can't do more than the UI, or less.

**Authentication.** Either a personal access token, `Authorization: Bearer ss_...` (make one on the account page,
or with `POST /auth/tokens` and a password), or the browser's session cookie. With the cookie, a write must be
JSON and come from this site (a foreign `Origin` is refused), which is the cross-site defence; uploads
(multipart) need a token. Operations that say "anyone" work signed out, and show more to people who may see more.

**Errors.** Every refusal is JSON with a stable `error` code for programs and a `detail` written for people, for
example `403 {"error": "submissions_closed", "detail": "Submissions for ... closed at ..."}`. Validation errors add
`fields`, per field. Hidden things answer 404, exactly like things that don't exist.

**Time.** Moments are ISO 8601 in UTC. Dates you send may carry an offset, or be the event's wall-clock time
(`2026-03-01T18:00`), which is how the event's own forms read them. Every deadline is judged by the server's clock,
and the deadline instant itself counts as closed.

**Lists.** Long lists are paged: `?page=` (from 1) and `?per_page=` (at most 200), answered with `count`, `page`,
`pages` and `results`.

**Limits.** Writes are limited to 120 a minute per person, on top of the portal's own limits (sign-ins, ballots,
comments...); a refusal is `429 slow_down`.

**Older routes.** A few routes under `/api/` predate this version and are kept because the DOGFOOD acceptance
checker calls them. They're listed under "Older /api/ routes", each naming its `/api/v1/` twin.

post.summary: Create an event
post.description:
Create an event. You become its organizer.

**Who:** platform organizer or admin.
**Same as, in the UI:** Create an event.
**Example body:** `{"name": ..., "starts_at": ..., "submissions_close_at": ..., "tracks": ["..."]}`

slug.description: Used in the address, e.g. /events/spring-hack-2026/. Leave empty to make one from the name.

starts_at.description: Teams can edit projects from this moment. ISO 8601 with an offset, or the event's wall-clock time as YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM.

submissions_close_at.description: Hard stop. Nothing can be created or edited after this. ISO 8601 with an offset, or the event's wall-clock time as YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM.

judging_ends_at.description: Judging ends. ISO 8601 with an offset, or the event's wall-clock time as YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM.

results_at.description: Winners announced. ISO 8601 with an offset, or the event's wall-clock time as YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM.

is_published.description: Unpublished events are only visible to organizers.

comments_enabled.description: Signed-in people can comment on projects in the gallery. Turn off to close every thread.

gallery_before_deadline.description: Off: submitted projects stay private to their team and the organizers until submissions close, so nobody can copy an early team's idea. On: they appear as soon as they're submitted.

tracks.description: Track names, one per track. Add descriptions and prizes afterwards.

post.summary: Something happened that the webhook listens for
post.description: One POST per audit-log entry the webhook's categories cover, sent once the change is saved (a rolled-back action is never announced). A 2xx answer within 5 seconds is a success; anything else is retried after 1 minute, 5 minutes, 30 minutes, 2 hours and 12 hours. Five given-up deliveries in a row switch the webhook off. To check a delivery: HMAC-SHA256 the string `<t>.<body>` with the webhook's secret, compare with `v1` in constant time, and refuse a `t` more than five minutes old.

parameters.name: Shipshape-Delivery
parameters.description: The delivery's id; the same on a retry.

default.description: Anything else, or no answer in 5 seconds, is retried.

refused.description: A refused attempt: a late edit, a rate limit.

Activity.description: One line of the audit log.

seed.description: The random seed, so the plan can be reproduced.

shortfall.description: Projects that couldn't get enough judges.

anyOf.description: A comment the organizers removed, as the public sees it.

weight.description: Relative weight; the rubric's weights needn't add up to anything.

response.description: The start of the receiver's answer.

DogfoodFixture.description: The shared DOGFOOD 2026 fixtures.json shape, which every portal in the hackathon loads. Ids are strings (evt_01, trk_01...); people are identified by email.

error.description: A short code, e.g. submissions_closed, not_found, slow_down.

fields.description: Per field, what's wrong with it.

Error.description: What every refusal looks like. `error` is stable, for programs; `detail` is written for people.

phase.description: Before kickoff, while submissions are open, after the deadline.

submissions_close_at.description: The deadline. The instant itself counts as closed.

gallery_before_deadline.description: Whether submitted projects are public before the deadline.

you.description: Your standing in this event, when you're signed in.

url.description: The invite link, while it's open.

Person.description: Someone, as others may see them.

PersonWithEmail.description: Someone, with their address: only shown to organizers and to themselves.

track.description: The track this prize belongs to, if any.

answers.description: Answers to the form's questions. Private ones only for the team and organizers.

is_public.description: Whether answers show on the public project page.

Question.description: A question the organizers added to the submission form.

details.description: Depends on the kind: the team and project, the prize, or for a judge how many projects they reviewed and scores_sha256 (never the marks).

record.description: What is signed. Never changes once issued.

signature.description: Ed25519, hex, over the record's canonical JSON.

SignedRecord.description: A signed record file: check it offline with records/verify.py, or POST it to /v1/records/verify.

invite_code.description: Only for the team's members and the event's organizers.

invite_url.description: The join link to send teammates.

prefix.description: The token's first characters, to recognise it.

max_votes.description: The most votes one ballot may give one project.

event.description: The event's slug; null for a platform webhook.

categories.description: What it hears: all, or the audit log's categories.

failure_streak.description: Given-up deliveries in a row; five switch it off.

secret.description: The signing secret (whsec_...). Only to the people who manage it.

id.description: The delivery's id (the Shipshape-Delivery header), to spot repeats.

type.description: What happened, e.g. project.submitted, or ping for a test.

WebhookPayload.description: What each delivery POSTs, signed with Shipshape-Signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<body>" keyed with the secret>. Refuse a t more than five minutes old.

per_page.name: per_page
per_page.description: How many per page (default 50, at most 200).

Invalid.description: Something in the request needs fixing; `fields` says what, per field.

SignIn.description: Sign in first, or the token is wrong or revoked (not_signed_in, bad_token).

Forbidden.description: Not allowed: not your event, not your role, outside the window (submissions_closed, judging_closed...), or a request from another site.

NotFound.description: Nothing here, or nothing you can see. The two are answered the same way.

NotJson.description: Writes with the session cookie must be JSON.

SlowDown.description: A rate limit: wait a moment (slow_down).

token.description: A personal access token from the account page or POST /auth/tokens.

session.name: session
session.description: The browser's session. Writes must be JSON from this site.
